dimension_assessments.summary: The export supplies n>0 and C>0 uniformly for every real C≤c1≤c2. Its witness construction chooses n>max(M,0) from the eventual RRA bound and retains that bound's threshold.

RRA rearrangement gives nU'+cU''≥0. The product derivative is c^(n−1)(nU'+cU''); C2 regularity supplies closed-ray continuity and interior differentiability. Monotonicity yields c1^n U'(c1)≤c2^n U'(c2), and positive denominators justify division.

The compared arguments are positive consumption levels and deriv utility is their ordinary marginal utility. The theorem does not substitute resources, assets or value marginals for consumption, and makes no change to household transition timing.

Visually inspected A93 printed 38–39/original PDF 39–40 and SE77 printed 161–162/original PDF 11–12. A93 Proposition 4 uses the power bound; SE77 (3.12)–(3.13) and its RRA discussion support the connection. Direct differentiation is the approved reconstruction, not certification of either source's full drift theorem.

The wrapper carries BASIC through HouseholdPrimitives. The helper requires only positive marginal utility, positive-domain smoothness and an eventual finite RRA bound; no further economic helper hypotheses enter.

Neither monotonicity nor the ratio conclusion is assumed. The utility premises are consistent: U(c)=c/(1+c) on c≥0 is bounded, increasing, strictly concave and has positive derivative with RRA=2c/(1+c)≤2.

The proof imports primitive definitions and Mathlib only. The diff adds the two D02 exports and their integration/audits; accepted economic proofs are unchanged and all predecessor restrictions remain operative.

Consumption ranges over real intervals, resources remain NNReal, and IncomeData retains an arbitrary probability law on compact labor support. The helper does not use income or replace iid histories with finite states.

C>0 and C≤c1≤c2 keep every differentiated argument strictly positive. Neither proof evaluates rightMarginalValue at zero or converts zeroRightMarginal; the separate ENNReal economic boundary object remains untouched.

Both proofs are pointwise real calculus. They form no expected marginal integral and perform no ENNReal-to-Real conversion. Positive c1 and U'(c2) are established before the divisions used to obtain the ratio inequality.

D02 concludes a deterministic inequality only. No distributional or moment convergence is invoked or inferred; the architecture's later drift and convergence objectives are not treated as consequences already proved here.

Neither signature assumes beta*R<1 or optimal-consumption positivity. Positive comparison arguments follow from the constructed C>0; positive marginal utility and C2 regularity are assigned SMOOTH/CURVATURE premises.

Both new proofs use ordinary calculus and algebra tactics. Their probes assert_no_sorry, and controller checks report no prohibited patterns or sorry dependencies; no axiom, native_decide or unsafe bypass appears.
The per-export axiom records list exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for both declarations. The controller's complete 398-record transitive union contains no additional axioms.

The inventory contains exactly the ratio theorem and power-monotonicity helper. Their signatures match source, and both receive #check, assert_no_sorry and #print axioms in the probe and Audit additions.

The Markdown ledger matches the existential signature, BASIC/SMOOTH/CURVATURE assumptions, derivative argument and helper. Its REVIEW_READY status agrees with the contract, and it explicitly excludes later drift claims.

UtilityCurvature expresses the intended eventual bound on −cU''/U'; UtilitySmooth supplies actual positive derivatives. The proof derives the marginal-utility ratio for the household's utility function, rather than assuming it or proving an unrelated numerical surrogate.

The inequality covers all ordered real consumption pairs above one threshold, including equality and the threshold itself. No finite grid, selected income law, conditional probability or stronger economic premise is introduced.

The only helper proves the analytic monotonicity needed for D02. Neither new declaration constructs drift bounds, invariant intervals, stationary distributions or later economic conclusions; scope verification reports PASS.

Independent calculus and source inspection support the exact D02 contract, with complete export audits and no unresolved substantive gaps. GREEN is justified for this gate only; compilation was not used as adequacy evidence.
